name: IEC exclusive-OR gate (rectangular form)
summary: Rectangular element marked =1: the output is active when one and only one input is active.
description: The =1 qualifier defines an exclusive-OR in the strict IEC sense: exactly one input must be active for the output to be active. For a two-input element this matches the familiar XOR truth table. For more than two inputs it is not the same as a cascaded parity function, which IEC writes as 2k+1.

On control drawings the =1 element appears in discrepancy checks, such as comparing a commanded position with a feedback contact, and in change-detection logic. The drafter should keep the element at two inputs unless the one-and-only-one meaning is truly intended.
The qualifier does not indicate timing tolerance. Discrepancy logic normally needs a delay element after the =1 box so that the alarm ignores normal transit time; that delay is a separate symbol.
readingNotes: For three or more inputs, read =1 as exactly one active, not odd parity.
Look for a following delay element in discrepancy logic.
drawingChecklist: Use =1 only where exactly-one behaviour is intended.
Use 2k+1 instead when odd parity is meant.
Show any discrepancy delay as its own element.
distinction: The 2k+1 odd-parity element gives the same result for two inputs but a different result for three or more.

facts.label: Multi-input caution
facts.value: Not equivalent to odd parity above two inputs
